name: commit_
summary: A curriculum tracker that uses a git-inspired completion loop to help independent developers keep momentum and finish courses.
problem: Independent learners can collect courses faster than they complete them. The product needed to make the next useful action obvious without turning progress tracking into another administrative task.
constraints: Keep the learning metaphor consistent across sessions, streaks, progress and milestones.
Support SQLite locally and PostgreSQL in production without maintaining separate domain models.
Make progress useful at a glance on desktop and mobile.
decisions: Model study sessions as commits and course completion as merging to main.
Center the interface on a repeatable loop: log, continue, review what is next and celebrate completion.
Use pacing and ETA feedback as guidance rather than punitive streak messaging.
implementation: Built the application with Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma and an interchangeable SQLite/PostgreSQL database setup.
Added roadmap, contribution graph, streak, XP, badge and email-digest surfaces around the same progress model.
Kept the dashboard, roadmap and streak views responsive and keyboard reachable.
outcome: The product is deployed publicly with the complete tracking loop available end to end.
verification: Confirm whether public usage or completion metrics can be published.
ownership: Product scope, data model, application code, interface, deployment and post-launch iteration.
architecture: Next.js application with a shared domain model, Prisma data access and an environment switch between SQLite for local development and PostgreSQL in production.
technicalHighlights: A single progress model powers the roadmap, streak, XP, badge and email-digest surfaces.
Pacing feedback is guidance rather than punitive streak messaging.
verifiedOutcomes: The product is publicly deployed with the tracking loop available end to end.

name: Orbit
summary: A relationship-management product that combines structured contacts, a visual graph, reminders and semantic search.
problem: Professional context is scattered across contact lists, notes and memory. Orbit brings relationship history, follow-ups and discovery into one queryable system.
constraints: Keep tenant data isolated at the database layer.
Combine graph exploration and semantic search without hiding ordinary contact workflows.
decisions: Use row-level security as the multi-tenant boundary instead of relying only on application filters.
Represent relationships with a D3 force-directed graph alongside conventional person records.
Use AI for semantic retrieval while retaining structured search and filters.
implementation: Implemented Google and LinkedIn OAuth, Stripe billing and Supabase persistence.
Added Gemini-powered semantic search, push reminders and bilingual interface support.
Deployed the web application on Vercel.
outcome: Orbit is deployed as a public product with authentication, persistence, search and billing flows.
verification: Confirm whether customer, revenue or relationship-volume metrics can be published.
ownership: Product scope, multi-tenant data model, authentication, search, billing, interface, deployment and launch operations.
architecture: Next.js application backed by Supabase PostgreSQL, with row-level security as the tenant boundary, structured contact workflows, semantic retrieval and a D3 relationship graph.
technicalHighlights: Tenant isolation is enforced at the database layer rather than relying only on application filters.
Semantic search complements, rather than replaces, structured contact search.
verifiedOutcomes: The product is deployed publicly with authentication, persistence, search and billing flows.

name: NexFlow
summary: An internal lead-management platform built to replace spreadsheet coordination with controlled workflows and an auditable record.
problem: Spreadsheet-based lead tracking made ownership, permissions and change history difficult to enforce across business teams.
constraints: Enforce field visibility on the server rather than merely hiding fields in the interface.
Generate conflict-free request codes under concurrent writes.
Support voice input and operational handoffs used by Arabic-speaking teams.
decisions: Strip restricted fields before responses reach unauthorized clients.
Generate request codes atomically in the persistence layer.
Record field-level before-and-after values for accountability.
implementation: Built role-based access control, audit history and real-time lead handoff surfaces.
Added Whisper transcription for Egyptian Arabic voice notes.
Integrated WhatsApp handoff cards into the lead workflow.
outcome: The deployed platform provides a structured alternative to the previous spreadsheet workflow.
verification: Confirm the number of business entities and lead records before publishing those metrics.
ownership: Workflow design, server-side authorization, persistence rules, audit history and operational handoff surfaces.
architecture: Internal B2B platform with server-enforced field visibility, atomic request-code generation, audit history and operational integrations.
technicalHighlights: Restricted fields are removed before unauthorized responses reach clients.
Field-level before-and-after values make operational changes auditable.
verifiedOutcomes: The deployed platform provides a structured alternative to spreadsheet-based lead coordination.
